title: GATE CS Topic Test — Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
titleEn: GATE CS Topic Test — Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following pipeline hazards is a TRUE data dependency?
questions.explanationEn: RAW (Read-After-Write) is a true data dependency because the second instruction genuinely needs the value produced by the first. WAR and WAW are false (name) dependencies resolvable by register renaming.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which type of cache miss occurs even in an infinitely large cache?
questions.explanationEn: A compulsory miss occurs on the very first access to a memory block, which cannot be avoided regardless of cache size or associativity.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A program consists of 2 × 10^6 instructions with an average CPI of 2.5 running on a 2 GHz processor. What is the execution time of the program in milliseconds?
questions.explanationEn: Execution Time = (IC × CPI) / Clock Rate = (2 × 10^6 × 2.5) / (2 × 10^9 Hz) = 2.5 × 10^-3 s = 2.5 ms.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: In DMA 'cycle stealing' mode:
optionsEn: The CPU is completely halted until the entire block transfer finishes
The DMA controller takes the bus for one memory cycle at a time to transfer a word, interleaving with CPU execution
The CPU executes each byte transfer via an ISR
DMA operates only when the CPU is in sleep mode
questions.explanationEn: In cycle stealing, the DMA controller steals single bus cycles from the CPU to transfer one word at a time, allowing the CPU to continue executing at a slightly reduced speed.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A direct-mapped cache has 64 blocks and block size 16 bytes. To which cache block index (0 to 63) does byte address 0x00001A5C map?
questions.explanationEn: Block number = 0x1A5C // 16 = 0x1A5 = 421. Cache block index = 421 mod 64 = 37 (since 64 × 6 = 384 and 421 - 384 = 37).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A floating-point unit optimization speeds up floating-point instructions by a factor of 4. If floating-point instructions originally accounted for 50% of total execution time, what is the overall speedup? (Round to 2 decimal places.)

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of a RISC architecture?
optionsEn: Variable-length instructions with memory-to-memory ALU operations
Large microprogrammed control ROM with complex addressing modes
questions.explanationEn: RISC designs use a load-store architecture (ALU operates only on registers), fixed-length instructions for simple decoding, and a large general-purpose register file.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which addressing mode is best suited for accessing elements of an array inside a loop where the base address is fixed and the index changes each iteration?
questions.explanationEn: Indexed addressing adds a fixed base address to an index register (which is incremented each iteration), directly yielding the effective address of A[i].

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A direct-mapped cache has a total data capacity of 16 KB and a block size of 64 bytes. How many cache lines (blocks) are in the cache?
questions.explanationEn: Number of cache lines = 16 KB / 64 B = (16 × 1024) / 64 = 256 lines.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the primary purpose of a daisy-chain priority interrupt mechanism?
optionsEn: To eliminate the need for an interrupt vector table
To allow multiple devices to share a single interrupt request line while resolving priority in hardware
questions.explanationEn: In daisy-chaining, the interrupt acknowledge (INTA) signal propagates serially through devices ordered by priority; the first requesting device intercepts INTA and supplies its vector.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about Tomasulo's algorithm and Reorder Buffers (ROB) are TRUE?
optionsEn: Reservation stations perform implicit register renaming to eliminate WAR and WAW hazards
Instructions can execute out of program order once their source operands are ready
A Reorder Buffer (ROB) allows instructions to commit in program order to support precise exceptions
Tomasulo's algorithm eliminates all RAW hazards without stalling
questions.explanationEn: Reservation stations tag operands to remove WAR/WAW (A), enable out-of-order execution (B), and ROB enforces in-order commit for precise exceptions (C). True RAW dependencies still require waiting for values (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A hard disk has an average seek time of 6 ms, rotates at 6000 RPM, and has a transfer rate of 50 MB/s (1 MB = 10^6 bytes). What is the average time (in ms) to read a contiguous 50 KB (50,000 bytes) file?
questions.explanationEn: 6000 RPM = 100 rev/s -> 1 rotation = 10 ms -> avg rotational latency = 5 ms. Transfer time = 50,000 / 50,000,000 = 1 ms. Total = 6 + 5 + 1 = 12.0 ms.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A CPU has a base CPI of 1.5 (assuming all memory accesses hit in cache). Every instruction requires 1 instruction fetch, and 30% of instructions also perform 1 data memory access. The unified cache has a 96% hit rate and a 25-cycle miss penalty. What is the effective CPI? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanationEn: Memory accesses per instruction = 1 + 0.30 = 1.30. Misses per instruction = 1.30 × 0.04 = 0.052. Stall cycles/instruction = 0.052 × 25 = 1.30. Effective CPI = 1.5 + 1.30 = 2.80.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A 2-way set-associative cache has 512 sets and a total data capacity of 32 KB. If physical addresses are 28 bits wide, how many bits are in the tag field?
questions.explanationEn: Total lines = 512 × 2 = 1024. Block size = 32 KB / 1024 = 32 bytes (5 offset bits). Index bits = log2(512) = 9 bits. Tag bits = 28 - 9 - 5 = 14 bits.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A 10-bit processor supports 3-bit register specifiers (8 registers). It has 10 two-register instructions and 32 one-register instructions. What is the maximum number of zero-register instructions that can still be encoded?
questions.explanationEn: Two-register instructions use 6 operand bits, leaving 4 opcode bits (16 prefixes). 10 used leaves 6 prefixes -> 6 × 8 = 48 one-register slots. Using 32 leaves 16 prefixes -> 16 × 8 = 128 zero-register instructions.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A system has an L1 cache (hit time = 1 cycle, local miss rate = 10%), an L2 cache (hit time = 10 cycles, local miss rate = 20%), and main memory (access time = 100 cycles). What is the Average Memory Access Time (AMAT) in cycles?
questions.explanationEn: AMAT = Hit_L1 + MissRate_L1 × (Hit_L2 + MissRate_L2 × MissPenalty_L2) = 1 + 0.10 × (10 + 0.20 × 100) = 1 + 0.10 × (10 + 20) = 1 + 3 = 4.0 cycles.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the code snippet:
I1: R1 = R2 + R3
I2: R2 = R1 + R4
I3: R1 = R5 + R6
Which exact set of data dependencies exists among I1, I2, and I3?
questions.explanationEn: I1 writes R1 and I2 reads R1 (RAW I1->I2); I1 reads R2 and I2 writes R2 (WAR I1->I2); I1 writes R1 and I3 writes R1 (WAW I1->I3); I2 reads R1 and I3 writes R1 (WAR I2->I3).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.topicTag: COA — Cache Conflict Misses in Matrix Traversal
questions.questionTextEn: A 4 KB direct-mapped cache with 64-byte blocks stores elements of a 64 × 64 array of 4-byte integers stored in row-major order starting at address 0. If a loop reads A[0][0], A[1][0], A[2][0], ..., A[63][0] (column-major traversal of column 0), how many cache misses occur?
questions.explanationEn: Each row is 64 × 4 = 256 bytes (4 cache blocks). Consecutive elements in column 0 are 256 bytes apart, so every single access falls in a different 64-byte block and causes a compulsory miss. Total misses = 64.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A 32-bit byte-addressable processor has a 128 KB 8-way set-associative cache with 64-byte blocks. What is the size of the cache tag directory in KB (storing only the tag bits, 1 KB = 1024 bytes)?
questions.explanationEn: Lines = 128 KB / 64 B = 2048. Sets = 2048 / 8 = 256 (8 index bits). Offset = 6 bits. Tag = 32 - 8 - 6 = 18 bits. Total tag size = 2048 × 18 bits = 36,864 bits = 4,608 bytes = 4.5 KB.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Computer Organization & Architecture (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A loop of 4 instructions executes 50 times (200 dynamic instructions total) on a 5-stage pipeline. Within each iteration, 1 stall cycle occurs due to a load-use hazard, and the backward branch at the end of each iteration is predicted taken (0 penalty for the first 49 iterations, 2-cycle penalty on the final loop-exit misprediction). How many total clock cycles does the loop take?
questions.explanationEn: Base cycles = 5 + 200 - 1 = 204. Load-use stalls = 50 × 1 = 50. Final branch misprediction = 2. Total = 204 + 50 + 2 = 256 cycles.
